title: A New Pickup System at the Community Library
subject: rla
passage:
The Westbridge Community Library lends more than books. Residents can borrow sewing machines, portable projectors, tool kits, and other equipment. Until last year, every item had to be collected from the service desk while it was open. People who worked late often reserved equipment but failed to pick it up before the reservation expired.

The library tested a locker system for smaller items. A borrower first reserves an available item online. Staff inspect the item and complete the checkout in the library system. Only after that checkout is recorded does the borrower receive a message with a locker number and a temporary code. The code opens the assigned locker until midnight on the pickup day. Returning equipment still happens at the service desk because staff need to inspect it before the loan is closed.

During the first two months, evening pickups increased and fewer reservations expired. The lockers did not solve every access problem, however. Larger tools could not fit, and some borrowers needed staff help learning how to operate unfamiliar equipment. For those loans, the service desk remained important.

Staff also discovered a communication problem. Several borrowers correctly received a locker number and a code but entered the locker number on the keypad instead of the code. The library first printed larger locker numbers on the doors, assuming that clearer signs would help. The error rate changed only slightly. Staff then redesigned the pickup message so that the code appeared under a bold label reading USE THIS CODE ON THE KEYPAD, while the locker number appeared under FIND THIS LOCKER. Wrong-code reports dropped sharply during the following month.

The library decided to keep both pickup methods. Lockers provide flexibility for routine loans that fit and do not require instruction. The desk provides assistance, handles large equipment, and checks returns. Staff members are now reviewing which items are appropriate for each method rather than trying to move every loan into lockers. They also plan to test whether a simple diagram in the pickup message can reduce first-time user questions.

Before expanding the pilot, staff also checked whether the lockers were being used by the same group of borrowers who already visited the library frequently. The first survey suggested a broader mix: some users were regular visitors, while others said evening pickup was the main reason they could complete the loan. Staff plan to repeat the survey before making larger purchasing decisions.

The pilot changed the library's original question. At first, staff asked whether lockers could replace the service desk for equipment loans. The results suggested a more useful question: which parts of the lending process can be automated without removing the human help that some loans require?

questions.prompt: Which step must occur before a borrower receives a locker code?
questions.explanation: The passage says the message is sent only after the checkout is recorded.
questions.rule: Words such as "only after" mark required order.

options.text: Staff record the checkout in the library system
The item is returned
options.whyWrong: “The item is returned” is placed at the wrong point in the sequence. Check what happens immediately before and after the target event.

options.text: The locker code expires
options.whyWrong: “The locker code expires” is placed at the wrong point in the sequence. Check what happens immediately before and after the target event.

options.text: The borrower visits the service desk to close the loan
options.whyWrong: “The borrower visits the service desk to close the loan” is placed at the wrong point in the sequence. Check what happens immediately before and after the target event.

questions.evidenceExcerpt: Only after that checkout is recorded does the borrower receive a message with a locker number and a temporary code.

questions.prompt: What is an important difference between locker pickup and service-desk pickup?
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts flexibility/automation with assistance and capacity.
questions.rule: Compare the same function - what each method can handle.

options.text: Only locker pickup involves borrowed equipment
options.whyWrong: “Only locker pickup involves borrowed equipment” does not fit the evidence and relationship required by this question. Recheck the exact wording of the passage and stem.

options.text: Lockers offer after-hours flexibility for suitable routine loans, while the desk can provide help and handle larger items
The service desk never checks returns
options.whyWrong: “The service desk never checks returns” assigns the two subjects’ features to the wrong sides of the comparison.

options.text: Both methods can handle every item in exactly the same way
options.whyWrong: “Both methods can handle every item in exactly the same way” focuses on a minor difference that does not answer the comparison being asked.

questions.evidenceExcerpt: Lockers provide flexibility for routine loans ... The desk provides assistance, handles large equipment, and checks returns.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion about the pickup-message redesign is best supported?
questions.explanation: Wrong-code reports dropped after the message clearly separated the two pieces of information.
questions.rule: Use the cause/effect relationship the text actually reports.

options.text: Making the locker numbers larger caused wrong-code reports to disappear
options.whyWrong: “Making the locker numbers larger caused wrong-code reports to disappe…” gives chronology without explaining the relationship the question asks about.

options.text: The keypad was replaced with a different device
options.whyWrong: “The keypad was replaced with a different device” shows that two things occurred together, but that alone does not establish causation.

options.text: Borrowers stopped using lockers entirely
options.whyWrong: “Borrowers stopped using lockers entirely” is an effect or result, not the cause the question asks for.

options.text: The clearer distinction between code and locker number was followed by a large drop in wrong-code reports

questions.evidenceExcerpt: Staff then redesigned the pickup message ... Wrong-code reports dropped sharply during the following month.

questions.prompt: What can the reader infer about the library staff?
questions.explanation: Staff test lockers, revise signage, redesign messages, keep both methods, and plan another test.
questions.rule: Look for a repeated pattern of decisions across the passage.

options.text: They are willing to revise a solution after observing how people actually use it
They want to eliminate all staff contact immediately
options.whyWrong: “They want to eliminate all staff contact immediately” conflicts with a specific detail in the passage.

options.text: They believe every error is caused by borrowers
options.whyWrong: “They believe every error is caused by borrowers” could be possible, but the passage does not provide enough evidence to support that conclusion.

options.text: They refuse to test new ideas
options.whyWrong: “They refuse to test new ideas” conflicts with a specific detail in the passage.

questions.evidenceExcerpt: The library decided to keep both pickup methods ... reviewing which items are appropriate for each method rather than trying to move every loan into lockers.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the pilot?
questions.explanation: The library keeps lockers for suitable loans and the desk for assistance, large items, and returns.
questions.rule: Synthesize the tradeoffs instead of selecting one isolated result.

options.text: Automation is useful only when it replaces every human task
options.whyWrong: “Automation is useful only when it replaces every human task” goes beyond the scope of the text. The evidence supports a narrower claim.

options.text: The most effective system may combine automated convenience with staff support for tasks that need judgment or assistance
Large equipment should never be loaned
options.whyWrong: “Large equipment should never be loaned” predicts an outcome the passage does not establish.

options.text: Pickup codes are the only important part of equipment lending
options.whyWrong: “Pickup codes are the only important part of equipment lending” relies too heavily on one detail instead of combining the relevant clues.

questions.evidenceExcerpt: which parts of the lending process can be automated without removing the human help that some loans require?

questions.prompt: How do borrower errors affect the design of the locker system?
questions.explanation: Observed errors become evidence that changes the communication design.
questions.rule: Describe the effect the problem has on the later design.

options.text: They have no effect on the pilot
options.whyWrong: “They have no effect on the pilot” connects details that the passage does not present as meaningfully related.

options.text: They cause staff to close the library
options.whyWrong: “They cause staff to close the library” reverses how the two ideas or events are connected in the passage.

options.text: They lead staff to revise how the message distinguishes the locker number from the code
They make large tools fit into lockers
options.whyWrong: “They make large tools fit into lockers” connects details that the passage does not present as meaningfully related.

questions.evidenceExcerpt: Staff then redesigned the pickup message ... Wrong-code reports dropped sharply during the following month.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
questions.explanation: A includes the pilot, revision, results, and final combined approach.
questions.rule: A summary keeps the important problem-solution-development chain.

options.text: All community libraries should replace service desks with lockers
options.whyWrong: “All community libraries should replace service desks with lockers” adds a claim that is not part of the passage’s main point or summary.

options.text: A library printed larger numbers on locker doors
options.whyWrong: “A library printed larger numbers on locker doors” captures only part of the idea and leaves out information the question requires.

options.text: A library tested equipment lockers, improved the system after observing access and communication problems, and kept lockers alongside staff service because the two methods meet different needs
The passage lists several kinds of equipment that residents can borrow
options.whyWrong: “The passage lists several kinds of equipment that residents can borrow” includes a detail but misses the broader idea the question asks you to identify.
